The trend

## What is the Come Back and Back dance, and where did it start?

The Come Back and Back dance is a short TikTok routine set to "Wyw My Sweetie", a Jersey Club track by nissi & 25Hzz. Choreographer @akanenmiyoshi posted the original on 17 September 2026, and K-pop idols joined in during October. The name comes from the hook, where the singer keeps calling someone to "come back and back".

People often misspell the song as "www my sweetie" or "why my sweetie", and many hear the hook as "come back and fly". They all point to the same trend.

The song

## Wyw My Sweetie: the song behind the trend

"Wyw My Sweetie #JerseyClub" is a Jersey Club track credited to nissi and 25Hzz, released by VBR on a four-track EP on 28 August 2026. Dancers use either its Slowed version or @akanenmiyoshi's original sound. The hook asks "my sweet, where you at" and keeps calling "come back and back", which gives the trend its name.

Jersey Club is a style of electronic club music that started in Newark, New Jersey, in the late 1990s and early 2000s. It's known for fast, bouncy kick patterns, which is why the dance is full of small bounces. Wikipedia

### Is the come back and back song made by AI?

Nobody has confirmed whether Wyw My Sweetie uses AI vocals. From 13–14 October 2026, posts on X and TikTok asked whether it was an AI song, and one TikTok making that claim passed 5.2M views. The credits list only nissi and 25Hzz, with no named singer.

Dancer Mai Linhi answered with a "non AI version" clip on YouTube. As of 29 October 2026, nissi, 25Hzz and VBR haven't commented. The dance itself was created and posted by choreographer @akanenmiyoshi.

## The Come Back and Back dance, beat by beat

The Come Back and Back dance is a 7-move routine of about 20 seconds, built on a small Jersey Club bounce. Timings below are approximate, and the AI video will follow the same flow rather than matching it frame for frame.

### 0–3 s: Knee pop

Bounce on the balls of your feet and knock one knee inward on the first beat.

### 3–6 s: Point up

Point one hand to the sky, then whip it down.

### 6–9 s: Head back

Tip your head back and sweep both arms over your head to cover your face.

### 9–12 s: Hip sway

One hand over your mouth, the other on your waistband, and sway your hips.

### 12–14 s: Shrug

Open both palms and shrug twice.

### 14–16 s: Wide rock

Drop into a wide stance, rock side to side and kick a knee toward the camera.

### 16–20 s: Hair to chest

Run both hands from your hair down to your chest and land back where you started.

The 7 moves fill about 20 seconds, so each one lasts 2 to 4 seconds. In duo clips, the second dancer often joins a few seconds in, while side-by-side duos and trios do the same moves in sync.

### The EU AI Act and AI-generated video

Article 50 of the EU AI Act applies from 2 August 2026. It requires deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates realistic video of people to disclose that the content has been artificially generated or manipulated. Evidently artistic, creative, satirical or fictional work has a lighter duty. It only needs a disclosure that does not hamper the display or enjoyment of the work. EUR-Lex: AI Act, Article 50

On Instagram and YouTube, turn on the AI label too. Meta: labeling AI content · YouTube Help: disclosing AI content

## Photo tips and what happens if something goes wrong

Come Back and Back AI will work best with a full-body photo of one person, facing the camera, in good light. The AI keeps what it can see, so a clear photo makes the biggest difference.

- Do: show your full body, or at least from the knees up

- Do: face the camera in good light

- Do: one person per photo

- Avoid: filters, sunglasses or a hand over your face

- Avoid: crowds or other people in the background
